name: table-count
description: Number of Drizzle pgTable() definitions across shared/. The mature-machine north star is a SMALLER schema (<=450 tables); today's count is far above it. This strict down-only ratchet makes the schema monotonic: adding a table fails CI until the baseline is deliberately bumped (a conscious 'yes we need this'), and every consolidation lowers the baseline toward the target. Founder-chosen 'strict' 2026-07-16.
lastBumpNote: 756 -> 757 on 2026-08-12: the Evidence Fabric's ONE table, evidence_claims -- the atomic truth primitive of the canonical architecture (Master Audit BI13). This bump is earned by a law, not a feature. Before it, provenance survived the FETCH and died at the WRITE: LookupResult (server/services/providers/types.ts) already carried provider, source, confidence, DataClassification, fetchedAt and sourceAsOf, and DATA_LICENSE_REGISTER already carried per-source rights -- then propertyEnrichment.savePropertyEnrichment() collapsed the entire result into a single properties.enrichment_data JSONB blob and OVERWROTE the previous one. No per-field provenance, no observation history, no conflict representation, no as-of reconstruction. Three of the fifteen canonical laws in shared/architecture/canon.ts were unsatisfiable as a direct result: evidence-known (2, every material assertion knows its evidence/provenance/freshness/uncertainty), unknown-is-valid (3, unknown and conflict must not be silently converted into certainty -- a missing flood-zone lookup rendering as 'no flood risk' is a fabrication check-no-fabrication.mjs cannot see, because no literal is invented, an absence is merely coerced), and decisions-immutable (6, a decision recorded today silently changes meaning tomorrow when the blob is overwritten). One row per source-backed assertion, APPEND-ONLY (no updated_at column -- a row that can be updated is a row whose history can be rewritten); corrections arrive as newer claims that out-rank older ones. It is ONE table and not five deliberately, because this ratchet's north star is a SMALLER schema: the source registry already exists as CODE (data-licenses.ts, DATA_LICENSE_REGISTER), the predicate vocabulary is a typed registry (shared/evidence/claim.ts, PREDICATES -- every entry read off a field a provider genuinely returns today, none invented), and the canonical resolved value is a PURE RECOMPUTABLE PROJECTION over the claims (BI14) rather than a materialised table -- so no evidence_sources, evidence_predicates or resolved_values table is needed, and none may be added without a measured need (Law 11). subject_id carries NO foreign key because subject_type may be 'parcel', which has no table yet (Parcel is conflated into properties); recording the parcel subject from day one makes the eventual Parcel/Property split a BACKFILL rather than a re-interpretation of history.
